source_paper.title: Distributed coding of choice, action and engagement across the mouse brain
source_paper.relationship: One original study session in its published NWB conversion; the benchmark is a secondary all-recorded-unit prediction method-sensitivity case, not a reproduction of the paper's residualized regional analysis.

source_handling: The single published NWB is copied byte-for-byte and SHA256-verified at image build. It is not converted or filtered by the staging step. No runtime download is required.

interpretation_notes.response_choice: The NWB trial description defines -1 as Right, +1 as Left, and 0 as No-go. This is the final registered response, which can differ from the initial wheel turn.
interpretation_notes.included: The source flag concerns disengagement; it does not include the paper's response-timing exclusions.
interpretation_notes.alignment: Trial timestamps share the session time base in seconds. response_time is retained as the registered-response alignment, not relabeled movement onset. A response-event overlap count does not establish whether any movement occurred in the stimulus window.
interpretation_notes.units: All stored clusters includes phy_annotations=1 multi-unit activity as well as values2 and3. The source paper generally used annotations>=2. Unit IDs are preserved in NWB row order; they are not row offsets.
interpretation_notes.source_conversion_limits: The unused wheel_moves series has twice as many timestamps as data values. The unused continuous wheel's stored rate appears to contain a sampling interval rather than Hz. This task does not repair or use those series to infer movement onset.
